angle: AI lets you shrink the central team and still accelerate change—if you productize transformation with agents and ruthless prioritization.
sourceTitle: The agentic transformation office: Redefining the economics of change
linkedinPost:
Big transformations don’t need big central teams anymore.

A recent McKinsey piece argues for an “agentic transformation office” — fewer people at the center, more AI agents driving execution across the org. That matches what I’m seeing on the ground.

In practice, this works when you treat change like a product: clear backlog, SLAs, usage analytics, and AI agents that own repeatable tasks (status rollups, variance flags, playbook nudges) with humans handling exceptions.

The win isn’t headcount optics. It’s cycle time and adherence. We’ve cut weekly status prep from 10 hours to 30 minutes, and surfaced risks 3 days earlier — because the agent watches data continuously instead of waiting for meetings.

Pitfalls: agent sprawl (too many tools, no owner), vague outcomes (busy dashboards, no behavior change), and no last-mile adoption plan. Start with 2-3 critical rituals to automate and give one leader P&L for the “change product.”

My take: measure the office by shipped decisions, not slide decks. If agents aren’t changing frontline behavior, they’re just theater.

Where could an agent replace a standing meeting next quarter? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy
